title: ADAS Sensor Calibrations Technical Standard: The Pre-Calibration Precheck and Alignment Validity
content:
## Clauses

**1. Manufacturer preconditions.** The ADAS Sensor Calibrations precheck verifies the manufacturer's preconditions before any attempt:
- the procedure document is on file, where the tier requires the manufacturer's procedure document;
- the pre-calibration scan is run, where the tier requires a pre-calibration scan;
- every diagnostic trouble code is resolved, where the tier requires it;
- the sensor mount is inspected, where the tier requires a sensor mount inspection;
- tires are at placard pressure, where the tier requires a tire pressure check;
- fuel is at least the tier's minimum fuel level, in percent;
- cargo is removed, where the tier requires the vehicle to be empty of cargo.

**2. Alignment.** Where the tier requires an alignment check, the most recent alignment check on the order is in spec and was made no more than the tier's alignment check validity days before the precheck. The tier's alignment check validity is 30 calendar days on every tier. Days are calendar days counted back from the precheck date, and a check made exactly that many days earlier is still valid.

**3. Out-of-spec findings.** An out-of-spec check must be corrected and checked again. On a customer-pay order the check posts an alignment check charge and a correction an alignment correction charge — this clause is **no longer in force**; it has been superseded by the current basis on which alignment work on a customer-pay order is billed. On an insurance claim repair the alignment is part of the repair order.

**4. Glass replacements.** For an order opened after a glass replacement, the windshield's safe drive-away time has passed before the precheck.

## How clause 2 is judged

- **Record.** The condition is read from the alignment checks recorded on this same calibration order: the most recent check is the one with the highest check number, and its result and date decide the condition.
- **Clock.** The clock runs back from the precheck date, in calendar days.
- **Boundary.** "No more than 30 days before" includes the 30th day: a check made exactly 30 days before the precheck is valid; one made 31 days before is not.
- **Result.** The most recent check must itself be in spec; an earlier in-spec check does not satisfy the clause when the most recent check is out of spec.
- **Scope.** The clause applies only where the tier requires an alignment check; Blind Spot Radar Calibration does not.

## Boundary cases (hypothetical dates, precheck on 31 March)

| Most recent alignment check on the order | Days counted back from the precheck date | Clause 2 |
|---|---|---|
| in spec, made 1 March | 30 | satisfied |
| in spec, made 28 February (non-leap year) | 31 | not satisfied |
| in spec, made 20 March | 11 | satisfied |
| out of spec, made 30 March (an in-spec check on 1 March before it) | — | not satisfied: the most recent check is out of spec |
